# BMS / DJMax Keysound Slicer UX Audit

## Scope and evidence
This audit distinguishes observed pain points from proposed DJMax Studio features. Numeric limits are format/tool-specific, not universal. Woslicer II/III's fetched references did **not** establish a numeric slice limit or a complete shortcut table; those are marked unknown rather than inferred.

## 1. Comparison table

| Tool | Workflow | Top 3 pain points | Max slices / snap | Export method |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sayaslicer | Load/drag audio; set offset and snap; place/preview markers; optionally zero-cross; copy BMSE or iBMSC clipboard, export keysounds, or save project. [GitHub README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features) | Zero-cross moves markers and can break iBMSC paste; BPM-change support is partial/hackish; historical >2GB files failed/lagged. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#important-notes) [Issue #5](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues/5) | Snap 1/1–1/192; iBMSC supports resolutions over 192th. No documented slice-count cap. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features) | Keysound export, keysound-list clipboard, BMSE/iBMSC clipboard; non-destructive project save is available, but final BMS still commonly needs files. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features) |
| Woslicer II | Load WAV; set BPM/offset/grid; add markers; preview; output numbered WAVs; set start WAV number; copy/paste BMSE clipboard into editor. ## 2. Problem inventory

### Timeline
- **P0 — No single source of truth between audio time and chart time.** Traditional workflows render, slice, then paste clipboard data and separately define numbered files; Woslicer/BMSE guides require matching BPM, cut order, start WAV number, and editor placement. A virtual `{sourceFile,startMs,endMs}` slice would remove this synchronization class. [Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/) [old Woslicer guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html)
- **P1 — BPM changes are weakly supported.** Sayaslicer calls its BPM-change support partial/hackish and lists proper grid/BPM import as planned; dtinth sound-slicer explicitly does not support BPM changes. [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features) [sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer)
- **P1 — Grid precision versus interchange is a trade-off.** Sayaslicer supports 1/1–1/192, but zero-cross can move markers and break iBMSC output; BMSE clipboard rounds to nearest 192nd. [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#important-notes)
- **P1 — Release tails and chopped boundaries are audible.** BMHelper guides tell users to increase minimum interval when releases/reverb collide; Woslicer III analysis identifies a one-sample reversal discontinuity as a pop-noise cause. [Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/) [Qiita](https://qiita.com/yuinore/items/79db943d2e3447adee71)

### Interface
- **P0 — Export ceremony is multi-stage and error-prone.** Users output hundreds of files, drag them into an editor at an exact definition start, then paste sequence data; Explorer ordering and both start positions must match. [Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)
- **P1 — Silent state/number errors are easy.** Woslicer III can have an apparently disabled Total Output until a filename appears; incorrect file order causes definitions to start from the wrong sample. [Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)
- **P1 — File management scales badly.** The sound-slicer example explicitly generates one file per event and prescribes a source folder plus `wav` child folder; Woslicer guides require deleting unwanted final silent slices and managing numbered outputs. [sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer) [Wix guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3)
- **P1 — Keyboard discoverability/platform friction.** Sayaslicer has extensive shortcuts because Woslicer does, but it also had macOS unsigned-app friction and a font-setting migration issue. [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#keyboard-shortcuts) [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)

### Settings
- **P1 — Boundary cleanup needs per-slice control.** Fruity Slicer exposes zero-cross, DeClick, Attack and Decay; Sayaslicer exposes zero-cross and fade/silent-tail features, but warns zero-cross changes timing. DJMax Studio should make Zero-X and fade explicit per slice with a visible timing delta. [Image-Line manual](https://www.image-line.com/fl-studio-learning/fl-studio-online-manual/html/plugins/Fruity%20Slicer.htm) [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features)
- **P1 — Automatic grouping has no universal optimum.** BMHelper/Mid2BMS settings for minimum interval, gate/velocity/pitch differences and chord treatment can either over-split or merge musically distinct events; Mid2BMS documents silence detection where too-small values create too many sounds and too-large values too few. [BMHelper guide](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html) [note guide](https://note.com/nakaiankow/n/n03caf5d703f9)
- **P2 — Snap choice should not silently alter interchange.** Sayaslicer distinguishes BMSE 192nd rounding from higher-resolution iBMSC output; Studio should show the quantized time and preserve the original ms boundary. [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#important-notes)

### Backend / format
- **P0 — Destructive export makes iteration expensive.** Existing tools create numbered WAVs and require a second editor import; dtinth’s melodic flow literally requires MIDI render -> WAV render -> slice -> clipboard paste. A virtual-slice backend keeps the source intact and makes undo/redo and re-cut cheap. [sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer)
- **P0 — Identifier-space overflow is real.** Typical BMS base-36 offers 1,295 usable keysounds; BMSE’s pilot base-62 expands to 3,843, while older implementations used narrower ranges. A Studio library should use stable internal IDs and validate target export limits before finalize. [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D음) [hitkey command memo](https://hitkey.nekokan.dyndns.info/cmds.htm)
- **P1 — Audio compatibility can crash old slicers.** Woslicer references report unsupported 24/32-bit or Studio One WAVs crashing; FL Studio 20.9 JUNK-header WAVs needed a patched build. Sayaslicer’s >2GB problem was fixed by changing backend and adding formats. [mid2bms wiki](https://wiki.mid2bms.net/%E4%BB%96%E3%83%84%E3%83%BC%E3%83%AB/woslicer) [Woslicer English README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/woslicerII-english) [Sayaslicer release](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/releases/tag/vb28b1af)
- **P1 — Playback semantics differ by target.** Older DJMAX-style single-track behavior can interrupt a previous sample; Technika 2 is described as changing to a non-interfering structure. BMS may restart the same sample ID, motivating over-definition. Studio needs explicit BMS/RESPECT/TECHNIKA playback modes and an overlap validator. [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D음)

## 3. What Sayaslicer did right vs Woslicer — keep these
1. Keep Woslicer-compatible keyboard muscle memory while accounting for keyboard layout. [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#keyboard-shortcuts)
2. Keep direct BMSE clipboard and iBMSC clipboard export, but present the target mode prominently. [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features)
3. Keep both common snaps and arbitrary 1/192 snapping, plus marker navigation, zoom and resnap-all. [Sayaslicer release](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/releases/tag/vb543f80)
4. Keep zero-cross, fade/silent-tail handling and preview, but expose the marker movement caused by cleanup. [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#important-notes)
5. Keep Woslicer III’s mouse-based direct chopping and its BMHelper clipboard bridge for automation-heavy or non-MIDI material. [Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)
6. Keep Woslicer’s preview-before-export loop and starting-number control, but replace the opaque ceremony with transactional Import to Studio. [old Woslicer guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html)

## 4. Top 10 recommendations
1. **P0: Make slices virtual until finalize.** Store source URI, start/end ms, source hash, and processing overrides; export WAV/OGG only on target finalize. This directly removes dtinth’s render/slice/paste round trip. [sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer)
2. **P0: Add one-click “Import to Studio” and round-trip IDs.** Import slices and chart notes into the project without clipboard, numbered-file, or Explorer ordering steps. Existing Woslicer/BMSE workflows require all three. [Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)
3. **P0: Provide target mode switcher BMS / RESPECT / TECHNIKA.** Validate ID limits, overlap semantics, and export behavior per mode; historical DJMAX capacity and Technika non-interference differ from BMS. [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82% کے음)
4. **P0: Add preflight before export.** Detect >target key limit, duplicate/restarted IDs, unrenderable formats, long files, missing sources, and out-of-grid markers. BMS 1,295 and DJMAX 1,023/2,047 reports justify visible validation. [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%음) [hitkey](https://hitkey.nekokan.dyndns.info/cmds.htm)
5. **P1: Build the proposed dual timeline.** Top chart preview with auto-created notes; bottom waveform with synchronized playhead, beat/bar and ms rulers, zoom and snap quantization. This addresses the split Woslicer/BMSE process and Sayaslicer’s planned proper grid display. [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features) [Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)
6. **P1: Make boundary processing non-destructive and inspectable.** Per-slice Zero-X, fade, normalize and tail policy; show original versus adjusted boundary and audible preview. Zero-cross movement and Woslicer pop noise are documented risks. [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#important-notes) [Qiita](https://qiita.com/yuinore/items/79db943d2e3447adee71)
7. **P1: Implement stable tempo maps.** Support BPM changes in grid, MIDI import, chart preview and export; never bake BPM assumptions into slice identity. Sayaslicer and sound-slicer both expose this gap. [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features) [sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer)
8. **P1: Add a searchable Slice Library and reuse suggestions.** Show identical/near-identical regions, target IDs, usage count, and whether reuse is safe under selected mode. BMHelper’s automatic repeated-note reuse and Woslicer manual reuse demonstrate the value. [Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/) [Wix guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3)
9. **P1: Make snapping explicit and reversible.** Offer 1/4 through 1/192 (and ms/free), show raw and quantized values, and preserve raw boundaries for finalize. Sayaslicer’s BMSE/iBMSC distinction proves this is not merely a cosmetic setting. [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features)
10. **P2: Robust cross-platform audio and recovery.** Decode common WAV bit depths, OGG/Opus and large files; show actionable conversion rather than crash; autosave projects and make undo/redo global. Woslicer crash workarounds and Sayaslicer’s backend migration are direct evidence. [mid2bms wiki](https://wiki.mid2bms.net/%E4%BB%96%E3%83%84%E3%83%BC%E3%83%AB/woslicer) [Sayaslicer release](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/releases/tag/vb28b1af)

### Evidence gaps
No accessible, citable PTSEQUENCER manual, no verified YouTube comments for exact Sayaslicer/Woslicer terms, and no fetched source established a hard Woslicer slice-count limit or complete shortcut table.
